shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, creating imbalance and reducing variety, which lowers my utility given my preference for balanced holdings.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 2 A, 0 B, 1 C, reducing variety and lowering my utility since I value diversity across goods. I'd rather keep balanced holdings or trade for something that improves variety, not decreases it.

Current inventory is balanced at 1/1/1. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C - a highly imbalanced bundle that reduces variety, which I value. I'd rather keep balance or trade for something that improves diversity, not reduces it.

I currently have equal quantities of A, B, and C (1 each). Trading away my C for B would just shift the imbalance to C without improving variety - I'd go from 1/1/1 to 1/2/0, which reduces diversity rather than helping it. Since I value variety, I should not give up my only unit of a good I already have equally distributed.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only B for another C would leave me with 1 A, 0 B, 2 C - reducing variety and making my bundle less balanced. Since I value variety, this trade would decrease my utility.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, C. Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 0 B and 3 C, creating a lopsided bundle (0,0,3 relative) which reduces variety value. I prefer to keep balanced holdings, so this trade decreases my utility.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would make my bundle worse rather than better.

Currently I have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, C. Trading away my only B for another A would leave me with 2 A, 0 B, 1 C, creating imbalance and losing variety, which lowers my utility since diminishing value applies to duplicates. Not beneficial.

Current bundle is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Trading away my only B for 2 A would leave me with 3 A, 0 B, 1 C - highly imbalanced and losing variety, which hurts my utility given I value variety. I'd rather keep balance or trade for something that maintains it.

I currently have equal amounts (1 each) of A, B, and C. Trading away my only C for another B would leave me with 0 C and 2 B, creating an imbalanced bundle, which is worse for me given my preference for variety.

I currently have equal amounts of A, B, and C (1 each), so trading away my B for another C would leave me with 2 C and 0 B, reducing variety and utility. Since I value variety, this trade would not improve my bundle.

Current inventory is 1/1/1, perfectly balanced. Giving up my only B to get 2 C would leave me with 1 A, 0 B, 3 C - a much less varied and thus less valuable bundle under my variety-preferring utility. This trade would reduce my utility, so I decline.

This trade would leave me with 0 A and 2 B, reducing variety instead of improving it. I currently have equal amounts of A and B (1 each), so trading away my only A for another B would make my bundle less balanced - going from (1,1,0) to (0,2,0), which decreases diversity value. I'd rather acquire C or keep balance between A and B.

This trade would give me 2×A and 0×B, resulting in a less balanced bundle (0 of a good) plus B is reportedly gaining value in the market, making it unwise to give up my only unit of B for an already-held good.

This trade would give me 3A, 0B, 0C - losing all variety and my only unit of B, which the market says is becoming scarce and valuable. Going from a balanced 1/1/0 to 3/0/0 reduces diversity significantly and gives up leverage on a good in high demand. I'd rather keep B or trade it for something that maintains variety, like C.

Currently I have 1 A, 1 B, 0 C - an even split except for C. Trading away my only B for C would just swap which good I have zero of, not improve variety. Also market signals suggest B is becoming scarce and valuable, so I should hold onto it rather than trade it away for equal value. I'd prefer to acquire C without giving up B, e.g., trading A for C instead.

This trade would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, going from a balanced (1,1,0) to an unbalanced bundle. Also, B is reportedly becoming scarce and valuable, so giving up my only B for C isn't favorable, especially since I'd have zero B afterward, hurting variety. I'd rather keep B or negotiate a trade that doesn't fully deplete it.

Current inventory is A:1, B:0, C:2. Trading away my only A for B would just swap which good I have zero of, not improving variety (I'd go from 1-0-2 to 0-1-2, same imbalance). Since B is becoming scarce and valuable, giving up my only A entirely for it leaves me with no A at all, which doesn't clearly improve my diversified position. I'd rather keep some A and try to acquire B without fully depleting A, or negotiate to keep both A and gain B via a different trade (e.g., trading C instead).
Currently I have 0 B and 2 C, so trading a C for a B moves me from (1,0,2) to (1,1,1), giving a perfectly balanced bundle. This increases variety utility significantly, outweighing the loss of one C.

This trade would leave me with A:1, B:1, C:0, trading away all my C for just 1 B. Giving up both units of C to go to zero is too extreme - I'd rather keep some C and get B more efficiently. A better trade would be 1 C for 1 B, keeping a balanced inventory (A:1, B:1, C:1) which maximizes variety value.

Currently I have only B (1) and nothing else. Trading away my only unit of B for A would leave me with 0 B and 1 A, just shifting which good I'm missing rather than increasing variety. Also, the market signals suggest B is becoming scarce and valuable, so I should hold onto it rather than trade it away for a 1:1 swap. I'd prefer to acquire C or additional A without giving up my only B.

This trade would leave me with 0 B and 2 A, giving up my only unit of a good that's becoming scarce and valuable, while ending up with a lopsided bundle (2 A, 0 B, 0 C). Since I value variety, I'd prefer to keep my B and acquire A and C separately rather than trade away my only B entirely for 2 A.

Currently I have 1 B and 0 A/C. Trading my only B for a C gives me variety (1 A=0, B=0, C=1 vs previous 0,1,0), which is equally diverse but the market signals B is becoming valuable, however since I'd still have zero variety either way, gaining C while losing B is neutral in count but the trade lets me diversify into C which I currently lack, similar marginal utility. Since it's a 1-for-1 swap between two goods I equally lack, and market suggests B is gaining value, I'll accept only if it improves diversity - here I go from having B only to having C only, same variety level (1 good), so no clear utility gain. I'll reject instead to preserve my B given rising demand.

Giving up my only B would leave me with 0 A, 0 B, 2 C - losing variety entirely and my only unit of a good that's becoming scarce and valuable. Better to keep B and seek a trade that adds variety without giving up my sole B.

Currently I have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C - very unbalanced. Trading 1 A (which I have plenty of) for 1 B (which I have none of) moves me toward a more balanced 1/1/1 bundle, increasing utility given my variety preference.

Giving up all my A (2 units) for just 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 B, 1 C - trading away all of one good for equal amount of another isn't a variety improvement. This would make me have 0 of A, which is worse for diversity. A better trade would be 1A for 1B to balance my holdings without depleting A entirely.

Trading away my only C would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just shifting the imbalance rather than improving variety. Current bundle (2,0,1) would become (2,1,0), which is not clearly better since I'd still have a zero. I'd prefer to keep C and acquire B without giving up my only unit of another good, or negotiate a trade that doesn't zero out C.

Currently I have only A (1 unit) and no B or C. Trading 1 A for 1 B gives me a more diversified bundle (1 A, 1 B), which increases utility given my preference for variety, since going from 0 to 1 B is more valuable than reducing A from 1 to 0 while still holding some A... actually this swaps A entirely, but having one of each of two goods rather than 1 of a single good matches the variety-seeking preference better."

Not beneficial.

Currently I have 2 A, 0 B, 1 C - very imbalanced. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me to 1 A, 1 B, 1 C, a perfectly balanced bundle, which maximizes utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 1B, 1C - trading a scarce-improving position for an even more imbalanced one. Currently I have 2A, 0B, 1C; giving away all my A to get just 1B overcorrects the imbalance and leaves A at zero. A better trade would be 1A for 1B to balance my holdings without depleting A entirely.

Trading away my only C (which I have least of, tied with B) for B just swaps which good I have 0 of, going from (2,0,1) to (2,1,0). This doesn't improve variety - both bundles have one good at 0. Since I'd rather build toward having all three goods, I should hold my C and seek a trade that gets me B without giving up my only C, or find a better ratio."
